title: W9 M1 -- Slide the Research panel in on a pointer open
description: Follow section '### M1 --' of docs/agent-work/2026-11-10-ui-wave-9/PLAN.md exactly, plus its 'Rules for every worker'. Verify: tests/w9-research-motion.spec.ts and the motion and research specs pass. Browser test port: PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=1444. No commits, no new packages, never run npm run build or a native screen script. Write the note docs/agent-work/2026-11-10-ui-wave-9/notes/M1.md.

review.note: Approved (CLAIMED; Chromium only). asideMotion.ts matches M1 step 3. It is a layout effect on 'shown'. It runs only when shown and wasPointer() are true and Reduce Motion is off. It calls play(el, translateX(--space-4 read as pixels, the plan's default) with opacity 0, to no transform with opacity 1, {speed:'base', easing:'out'}), cancels on cleanup and does nothing on close. The signature matches the T0 interface; there is no App.tsx edit. Spec check (the coordinator asked whether the opacity fix loosened it): the pointer case still asserts exactly one animation on .research-aside, duration 180, the property set exactly [opacity, transform], first frame opacity 0 with translateX, end state no transform and opacity '1', and an unchanged .writer-scroll width on the first frame. Number(first.opacity) only normalises the keyframe value's type; nothing was loosened. Other cases: palette open none, Reduce Motion none, close none. Gap, not blocking: the plan names 'keyboard or command palette' and only the palette path is tested; the hook gates on the same wasPointer() either way. Relied on the worker's 4/4 plus motion and research runs; I did not rerun the browser spec.
